text: I have heard it shrewdly said that to one man you may impart anything, since, unless you have been led to commit yourself by writing, your denial will go as far as his assertion. Shun writing, therefore, as you would a rock, for there is nothing so damning as a letter under your own hand.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
